note: The port's per-dispatch spans at 1080p, to answer a question the 1440p profile cannot: does the port's arithmetic scale with the pixel count? The worker's own per-frame line says no. From the same frame of two runs of the same fixture, 1440p (r2026-11-07-video-workerlog frame 299) reads proxy 2.2, network+composite 11.5, readback 3.6, reply 2.0; 1080p (r2026-11-08-1080p-video frame 299) reads 1.7, 9.9, 1.7, 0.7. Readback and reply scale roughly with pixels and proxy nearly so - but network+composite falls only 11.5 -> 9.9, 14%, for 44% fewer pixels. If the network were pixel-bound it would be ~6.5. NGX scales: 7.1 ms at 1440p, 4.6 at 1080p. So the port's network looks like it carries ~5 ms that does not depend on resolution, and that would make it the largest single item in the project - bigger than the 1.37x this plan calls the NGX gap, and the reason the gap at 1080p is 9.9 against 4.6 (2.15x) while at 1440p it is 11.5 against 7.1 (1.6x). What this run settles: compare the summed per-dispatch spans at 1080p against 1440p's 9.749 ms (r2026-11-03-profile, idle card). Linear would be ~5.5 ms. If the sum lands near 9, the spans themselves have a fixed component and the kernels are the target. If it lands near 5.5, the arithmetic is fine and the 9.9 wall clock is ~4.4 ms of gap between dispatches - a CPU-side submission cost, which is a completely different fix and would make the kernel table a dead end. Also read: which kernels hold the fixed component, since the same names at 1080p and 1440p is the signature of a cost that is not area-bound. One caveat, from the plan's own note: this route disables chaining, so its total is a sum of spans and must not be compared against a frame time - only against the other profile.
